capabilities.apply_patch_note: Responses API only. Live-verified 2026-08-22 on gpt-5.1 (create_file/update_file/delete_file, streaming and not); gpt-4o-mini refuses it with a typed invalid_request_error.
capabilities.code_interpreter_note: Responses API code_interpreter tool, container: {type: auto}. Live-verified 2026-08-22 on gpt-5.1, streaming and not. outputs is null even on a successful run; the human-readable result arrives as the following message's text, not on the call item. A generated file surfaces only as a container_file_citation annotation needing a further authenticated download, not yet built.
capabilities.custom_tool_note: Responses API custom tool ({type: custom, name, description}, no JSON Schema). Live-verified 2026-08-22 on gpt-5.1, streaming and not: the model's call arrives as {type: custom_tool_call, call_id, name, input}, input a plain string; the reply is {type: custom_tool_call_output, call_id, output}. Streaming adds response.custom_tool_call_input.delta/.done, redundant with the terminal event same as apply_patch and code_interpreter.
capabilities.tool_search_note: Responses API tool_search ({type: tool_search}, hosted mode), gpt-5.4+ only. Deferred function tools set defer_loading: true. Live-verified 2026-08-22, streaming and not: tool_search_call/tool_search_output arrive as ordinary output items (whole, no dedicated streaming deltas), then the discovered tool's function_call/function_call_output round-trips the same way a non-deferred one does; replay needs no special handling.
capabilities.reasoning_effort_note: Maps to the Responses reasoning.effort field. Verified live 2026-08-14 on gpt-5-nano.
capabilities.prompt_caching_note: TextInput(cacheable=True) sets prompt_cache_options.mode=explicit at the top level and prompt_cache_breakpoint: {mode: explicit} on that content block. Automatic (implicit) caching already runs above ~1024-2048 tokens with no marker at all; the explicit marker is an optional reliability aid on top of that, not a requirement. cache_ttl_seconds is not a concept on OpenAI's side and is silently unused.

capabilities.realtime_note: The Realtime API (GA session shape). Text and audio output modalities both verified live 2026-08-14; usage arrives in response.done.
capabilities.live_note: gpt-live full-duplex voice on POST-created WebSocket sessions at /v1/live/sessions (its own endpoint, not the Realtime API). The model rides the session-config message, and reasoning plus tool use are delegated to a backend Responses model billed separately from the per-second voice session. Served by live(). Partially probed 2026-09-12 on a gpt-live-1-entitled key (two rounds): endpoint reachable and entitled, socket connects and authenticates, model id accepted, opening handshake confirmed (first frame session.start carrying the config; delegation rides delegation.responses). Round 2 raw-frame tap: the delegated backend Responses stream arrives nested in a response.event envelope (unwrapped here). Rounds 3-4: gpt-live has no output_modalities key (rejected both as a per-response wrapper and as a session field), so none is sent; audio output rides the audio.output block. Probed end to end 2026-09-12: a full voiced audio turn works. Caller audio is session.input_audio.append and the turn ends with session.input_audio.mute (gpt-live's own vocabulary, not the Realtime input_audio_buffer.* or output_modalities). The model voices back over top-level session.* frames (session.output_audio.delta, session.output_transcript.delta, session.input_transcript.delta); billing is incremental via session.usage.updated (no turn-complete or session-ended frame on the audio path). The text-input path streams the delegated Responses events in a response.event envelope, which the translator unwraps. A full release probe still gates the ship.
capabilities.batch_generation_note: Files API upload (purpose=batch, JSONL lines targeting /v1/responses) then POST /batches with completion_window 24h (the only accepted value); one model per input file; up to 50000 requests / 200MB per file at a 50% token discount. Results and per-line errors are separate downloadable files; output kept 30 days. Statuses validating/in_progress/finalizing/completed/failed/expired/cancelling/cancelled. Live-verified end to end 2026-09-02, including a per-org failure mode where batch validation cannot read a file the same key uploads and reads back — provider-side project state, fixed by a fresh project.
capabilities.batch_embeddings_note: Same file-and-batch loop with JSONL lines targeting /v1/embeddings, one input per line. Live-verified 2026-09-02.
capabilities.transcription_note: Multipart POST /v1/audio/transcriptions, live-verified 2026-09-02. whisper-1 takes response_format=verbose_json + timestamp_granularities[]=word and returns duration/language/words (seconds, no per-word confidence); the gpt-4o transcribe family refuses verbose_json with a 400 naming json/text, so it returns text only, with token-billed usage. gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize has its own diarized_json format returning speaker-labelled segments, not words - not wired; diarize=True refuses on this provider. 25MB file limit per the docs.
capabilities.reasoning_effort_minimal_note: The Responses API defines a 'minimal' effort level (verified live 2026-08-14).
capabilities.streaming_only_transcription_families_no: OpenAI's model list mixes transcription models that serve only the realtime socket in with the ones the stored-file endpoint takes, and nothing in the listing tells them apart. POST /v1/audio/transcriptions answers 404 'Invalid URL' for gpt-live-transcribe and gpt-realtime-whisper, while gpt-transcribe, whisper-1, and the whole gpt-4o transcribe family (gpt-4o-transcribe, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe, their dated snapshots, and gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize) answer 200 (all nine live-probed 2026-09-10). Matched as substrings of the lowercased id so a later snapshot of the same family is covered; a release probe checks both directions, so a family wrongly listed here fails loudly rather than hiding a model that works.

capabilities.code_interpreter_note: code_execution_20250825 tool, needs the anthropic-beta: code-execution-2025-08-25 header (sent only on a request that asks for it). Live-verified 2026-08-22 on claude-opus-5, non-streaming: the model invokes an internally-mapped bash_code_execution server tool (server_tool_use + bash_code_execution_tool_result blocks), normalized here; only that pair is normalized, a chained text_editor_code_execution call falls through to UnknownOutput. Non-streaming only in this increment: a streaming call still completes with the correct final text, but its code/output blocks are silently dropped rather than surfaced, since Anthropic's streaming shape for this tool has not yet been live-probed.
capabilities.tool_search_note: tool_search_tool_bm25_20251119 (natural-language search variant), no beta header needed. Deferred client tools set defer_loading: true. Live-verified 2026-08-22 on claude-opus-5, streaming and not: search runs as server_tool_use/tool_search_tool_result blocks, the discovered tool's tool_use/tool_result round-trips like any ordinary tool call. Confirmed live that omitting the server_tool_use/tool_search_tool_result blocks entirely on replay still works (the API tolerates it despite docs recommending they ride back unchanged), so KeyCall treats them as trace-of-work, same as web_search's own blocks.
capabilities.reasoning_effort_note: Maps to output_config.effort; a top-level effort field is refused. Verified live 2026-08-14 on claude-opus-4-5.
capabilities.prompt_caching_note: TextInput(cacheable=True) sets a cache_control: {type: ephemeral, ttl} block on that content block; a system TextInput switches the system field from a joined string to a block array only when a cache marker is present. Anthropic is the one provider where caching doesn't happen at all without this marker. cache_ttl_seconds must be 300 ("5m", default, no extra cost) or 3600 ("1h", billed at double the base input rate) — any other value is refused before the network call rather than rounded.
capabilities.schema_enforcement_note: output_config.format {type: json_schema, schema} on /v1/messages; the answer arrives as an ordinary text block (text_delta when streaming) and composes with caller tools and web_search. Live-verified 2026-09-10 on every model the test key lists, claude-fable-5-1 down to the dated 4.5 snapshots. The forced-tool alternative (a synthetic tool plus tool_choice type tool) is refused by claude-fable-5-1 with a 400.

capabilities.web_search_note: Served by the $web_search builtin_function on chat completions: the search runs server-side, but the model answers finish_reason tool_calls and the caller must echo the call's arguments back as a tool message before the answer arrives. KeyCall runs that echo loop internally, so web_search=True behaves like every other provider. No structured citations are returned. Verified live 2026-08-14 on kimi-k2.6.
capabilities.batch_generation_note: OpenAI-shaped file-and-batch loop, /v1/chat/completions lines only, one model per file enforced at upload, request bodies validated line by line at upload (a defective line rejects the file naming the line number). Batch jobs price at 60% of the live rate on the models its batch pricing page lists. Slow: a 2-request batch took 747s (verified 2026-09-02). Output lines wrap deeper than OpenAI's ({response: {request_id, status_code, body}}, status_code 0 on success). Live-verified end to end 2026-09-02.

capabilities.code_interpreter_note: Rides POST /v1/responses like web_search and reasoning_effort, reusing OpenAI's adapter and parser. Live-verified 2026-08-22 on grok-4.3, non-streaming and streaming: same code_interpreter_call item type as OpenAI but no container_id field, and outputs is a non-null logs list that is often empty even when the code printed something. No confirmed mechanism to retrieve a generated file at all (unlike OpenAI's opaque reference or Gemini's inline bytes).
capabilities.reasoning_effort_note: Rides POST /v1/responses as reasoning.effort, which binds (reasoning token counts follow the level, measured 2026-08-14); the chat-completions reasoning_effort field answers 200 without binding, so requests naming an effort are routed to the responses surface.
capabilities.schema_enforcement_note: chat completions accepts response_format={type:json_schema, strict:true} and enforces it: a valid schema returns conforming JSON, a malformed schema type 400s with 'Schema validation failed', and the json_object floor returns free-form JSON that ignores the field names (live-verified 2026-09-08 on grok-4.6). Enforcement rides the openai-compatible json_schema wire, so xai belongs with moonshot and perplexity, not with the native-adapter providers.
capabilities.image_input_note: Inputs below 512 total pixels are refused with code invalid_image.
capabilities.embeddings_note: POST /v1/embeddings exists but no embedding model is offered; language models are refused by name. Verified live 2026-08-13.
capabilities.video_download_note: Finished videos are served from vidgen.x.ai as unauthenticated, unsigned URLs: the URL itself is the only secret, and no credential is ever sent to that host.
capabilities.realtime_note: Grok Voice speaks the Realtime API with the pre-GA session shape (modalities, not output_modalities) and is voice-only: a text-modality update is echoed as accepted but the answer still arrives as audio plus transcript, and no usage is reported. Verified live 2026-08-14.
capabilities.batch_generation_note: Its own dialect: create a named batch container, add batch_requests (each wrapping a chat_get_completion body) in a second call, poll counters (num_pending/num_success/num_error/num_cancelled — no status string; the state is derived), fetch paginated results whose batch_result.response.chat_get_completion is a standard chat.completion. Only a subset of models is batch-eligible; an ineligible model rejects the whole add call atomically. grok-4.3 verified live end to end 2026-09-02, processed in 13s. Media result URLs expire after an hour; discounts are per model page.

retired_models.note: Absent from xAI's model docs with no published retirement date (xAI announces retirements by email/console); refusal live-verified 2026-09-04 (400 'Model not found'). No provider-named replacement. The May 2026 retirement slugs (grok-3, grok-4-0709, grok-code-fast-1, the grok-4-fast family, grok-3-mini) stay out: xAI redirects them to live models and they answer 200, verified the same day.

assemblyai.model_discovery_note: AssemblyAI exposes no model-list endpoint; the streaming model set is maintained here. The list call hits GET /v2/transcript?limit=1 purely to validate the credential (200 with a valid key, 401 otherwise, verified live 2026-08-28).

assemblyai.retired_models_note: No retired ids as of 2026-09-04: the changelog's deprecated speech_models values (universal-3-pro, universal) still complete jobs end to end, verified live that day.

capabilities.streaming_transcription_note: Universal Streaming v3 over wss://streaming.assemblyai.com/v3/ws (a different host from the REST API, hence the full URL in the operation path), bare key in the Authorization header. Live-verified 2026-08-28: Begin/Turn/Termination frames, interims as a growing transcript on one turn_order, finals as end_of_turn with per-word ms timings, Termination reporting audio_duration_seconds. Single audio channel only. Sessions auto-close after 3 hours.
capabilities.transcription_note: Job-shaped, live-verified 2026-09-02: raw-binary POST /v2/upload answers upload_url (readable only by AssemblyAI, same account), POST /v2/transcript takes audio_url plus speech_models as an array (the accepted spelling; the legacy singular speech_model echoes null) and speaker_labels, then GET /v2/transcript/{id} polls queued/processing/completed/error. Completed carries text, overall confidence, audio_duration (integer seconds), language_code (ISO-639-1), and words[] with millisecond start/end, confidence, and speaker letters under speaker_labels.
capabilities.streaming_diarization_note: Streaming diarization rides the v3 socket as speaker_labels=true (with an optional max_speakers, 1-10); each finalized word in a Turn frame carries a `speaker` string. Live-probed 2026-09-08 on two-voice audio: words came back labelled 'A' and 'B'.

deepgram.model_discovery_note: Deepgram exposes no model-list endpoint on the key's own scope; the streaming model set is maintained here. The list call hits GET /v1/auth/token purely to validate the credential (200 with a valid key, 401 otherwise, verified live 2026-08-28).
deepgram.retired_models_note: No retired ids as of 2026-09-04: the docs keep every legacy tier (nova, enhanced, base, whisper) usable and the changelog records no model retirement.

capabilities.streaming_transcription_note: wss://api.deepgram.com/v1/listen with Token-scheme Authorization. Live-verified 2026-08-28: Results frames with is_final/speech_final, per-word timings in float seconds (normalized to ms), punctuated_word alongside the raw word, terminal Metadata frame reporting duration. No session-begin frame at all; a successful connect is the only accept signal. channel_index present on every result.
capabilities.transcription_note: POST /v1/listen with a raw binary audio body (or JSON {url}), query params model/punctuate/language/diarize, live-verified 2026-09-02 on nova-3 (bytes path): metadata.duration + request_id, results.channels[].alternatives[] with punctuated transcript, overall confidence, words[] carrying start/end seconds, per-word confidence, punctuated_word, and speaker (int) + speaker_confidence under diarize=true. 2GB file limit, 10-minute processing cap per the docs. The JSON {url} path also live-verified 2026-09-02 against a public mp3.
capabilities.streaming_diarization_note: Streaming diarization rides the listen socket as diarize=true; each word inside a final Results frame carries an integer `speaker`. Live-probed 2026-09-08 on two-voice audio. diarize_model=v2 is prerecorded-only and 400s on this socket.

elevenlabs.model_discovery_note: GET /v1/models is authenticated (401 invalid_api_key on a bad key, 401 missing_permissions on a key without the models_read scope, both verified live 2026-08-31) and lists TTS and voice-conversion models with capability booleans; STT models are absent from it, so the streaming model set is maintained here. The test key needs models/user/voices read scopes plus text-to-speech and speech-to-text access.

models.wires_note: Streaming live-verified 2026-08-31; the prerecorded endpoint refused it live 2026-09-03 (invalid_model_id, naming scribe_v1/scribe_v1_experimental/scribe_v2 as valid).
Prerecorded live-verified 2026-09-02; the realtime endpoint refused it live 2026-09-03 (invalid_request, close 1008).

retired_models.note: ElevenLabs changelog 2026-06-08 (removal extended from 2025-12-15); refusal live-verified 2026-09-04 (400 unsupported_model). scribe_v1 and scribe_v1_experimental stay out: both still pass model validation live the same day.

capabilities.speech_generation_note: POST /v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id} with the voice id in the path, so a voice is required and there is no provider-side default; body carries text and model_id, response is the audio bytes themselves (audio/mpeg at the default output format). Bad voice and bad model ids both return 400 status invalid_uid; a missing text field returns 422 whose detail is a list, not the object every other error uses. Verified live 2026-08-31 on eleven_flash_v2_5.
capabilities.streaming_transcription_note: wss://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/speech-to-text/realtime, xi-api-key header. Audio goes as JSON messages ({message_type: input_audio_chunk, audio_base_64, sample_rate, commit}), not binary frames; events are session_started / partial_transcript / committed_transcript / committed_transcript_with_timestamps (per-word start/end in seconds, logprob confidence, speaker_id). A bad key opens the socket and then sends an auth_error event before closing, unlike the HTTP 401 path. The server never closes after a commit — the client owns termination — and no event reports billed audio duration. scribe_v2_realtime is the accepted model_id (scribe_v1 is rejected on this endpoint). Verified live 2026-08-31.
capabilities.voices_note: GET /v1/voices returns the account's voices ({voices: [{voice_id, name, category, ...}]}); 21 premade voices on a fresh free account. Needs the voices_read scope. Verified live 2026-08-31.
capabilities.transcription_note: Multipart POST /v1/speech-to-text with model_id and one of file/source_url (never both), live-verified 2026-09-02 on scribe_v2 (bytes path): text, language_code (ISO-639-3) + language_probability, audio_duration_secs, transcription_id, words[] mixing types word/spacing with start/end seconds, per-word logprob, and speaker_id under diarize=true. 5GB file limit, 100ms minimum, <=5 channels per the docs. The source_url path (a file-less multipart form) also live-verified 2026-09-02 against a public mp3.
capabilities.streaming_diarization_note: The realtime socket takes no diarization parameter and never fills the field: committed_transcript_with_timestamps words carry a speaker_id key that stayed null for every word, with and without a diarize param (live-probed 2026-09-08, 18 words, scribe_v2_realtime). Prerecorded diarization is unaffected and still reports speaker ids.

service_categories.name: geocoding
service_categories.note: v4beta surface chosen over the legacy maps.googleapis.com endpoint because it takes the X-Goog-Api-Key header, which the legacy one refuses (REQUEST_DENIED with the key in a header, OK with it in the query string; both live-probed 2026-09-10). $5.00 per 1000 after 10000 free monthly calls (Essentials tier, pricing page read 2026-09-10).

service_categories.name: places
service_categories.note: Needs an X-Goog-FieldMask header naming the response fields; probes request places.id only, the cheapest mask. Live-probed 2026-09-10. $32.00 per 1000 after 5000 free monthly calls (Pro tier, pricing page read 2026-09-10).

service_categories.name: directions
service_categories.note: Google's Routes API; the category keeps the neutral name so another provider's turn-by-turn service can join it. Needs an X-Goog-FieldMask header. Live-probed 2026-09-10. $5.00 per 1000 after 10000 free monthly calls (Essentials tier, pricing page read 2026-09-10).

google_maps.error_shape_note: Category endpoints answer google.rpc envelopes: a bad key is HTTP 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT "API key not valid"; an API not enabled on the key's project is HTTP 403 whose message names the API and carries the console enable URL (both live-probed 2026-09-10).

service_categories.name: realtime
service_categories.note: Host is the caller's per-project base_url (https://<project>.livekit.cloud). Auth is a stdlib-minted HS256 JWT: iss = api_key, signed with api_secret, video.roomList grant, sent as Bearer. 200 with a rooms array (empty on a fresh project) validates the pair; a bad signature answers 401 with a plain-text body, a valid signature without the grant answers 401 with a Twirp JSON body, so wrong-secret and missing-permission are distinguishable. All live-probed 2026-09-10.
